questions.question: Why must an update include the current CouchDB `_rev` value?
options: It selects the shard count for the database
It proves which leaf revision the writer observed so stale updates can be rejected
It permanently orders every business event by time
It encrypts the document body
questions.explanation: CouchDB uses `_rev` for optimistic concurrency. A stale token causes a 409 on a single database instead of silently replacing a newer leaf.

questions.question: Two disconnected databases update the same base document and later replicate. What should the application expect?
options: Both branches can be preserved as conflicting leaf revisions
The source database always overwrites the target
Replication rejects both revisions with 409
CouchDB automatically merges every JSON field
questions.explanation: Independent databases can accept concurrent descendants. Replication preserves the branches, chooses a deterministic winner for default reads, and leaves business resolution to the application.

questions.question: What does CouchDB's deterministic winning revision guarantee?
options: The winning branch contains the correct business decision
The branch with the newest wall clock always wins
Replicas can agree on which branch a normal read returns by default
All losing fields are merged into the winner
questions.explanation: The winner gives replicas a consistent default read result. Revision ordering does not encode domain authority, so the application must still inspect and resolve conflict leaves.

questions.question: What is the safest response to a 409 from a business update?
options: Retry the identical stale body until it succeeds
Delete the document and recreate it
Increase the cluster's shard count
Fetch the current document and re-evaluate the operation against the new state
questions.explanation: A 409 means another revision superseded the version you observed. Re-read, validate the current state, and reapply the domain operation only if it is still valid.

questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes CouchDB cluster replicas from database replication?
options: They are identical names for the same background job
Cluster replicas copy shard ranges inside one logical database; replication synchronizes revision trees between databases
Database replication creates relational read replicas
Cluster replicas eliminate document conflicts
questions.explanation: The cluster uses shard replicas to serve one logical database. Replication is a checkpointed source-to-target synchronization between independently addressable databases.

questions.question: Why can a partition-scoped query be cheaper than a global query in a partitioned database?
options: It can read one shard range instead of consulting every shard
It bypasses every index
It disables document revisions
It stores all tenants in one document
questions.explanation: Documents sharing a partition key are colocated in one shard range. Partitioned views and Mango queries can use that locality instead of fanning out across all q shards.

questions.question: What is the best release-time evidence that a Mango query uses the intended index?
options: The selector is valid JSON
The database has at least one design document
`_explain` names the expected index and a production-shaped load test meets the service target
The query returns fewer than 25 documents
questions.explanation: `_explain` exposes the selected index, while load testing verifies the real cost of data volume, cardinality, cache state, and concurrent writes.

questions.question: Why is CouchDB replication not a replacement for independent backups?
options: Replication can copy accidental deletes and corrupt application writes to the peer
Replication never transfers attachments
Backups are required to create Mango indexes
A replicated database cannot be queried
questions.explanation: Replication synchronizes active changes, including harmful ones. Recovery requires an independent, tested copy that is not automatically following the same deletion or bad write.
